beats.say: Here is a customer on the SkyDesk site. She booked this morning by mistake, and asks the assistant to cancel and refund her.
beats.do: open the chat, type the RSK7FT request, send

beats.say: Watch the activity strip. It verifies her name and card, looks up the booking, checks the twenty four hour policy, and quotes the refund.
beats.do: wait for the reply, highlight the step strip

beats.say: Then it stops. This approval card shows one hundred forty seven dollars and eighty six cents, line by line, with the policy rule behind each line.
beats.do: highlight the amount, then the breakdown lines

beats.say: I approve it as the supervisor. Only now does the agent cancel the booking and confirm the exact amount to the customer.
beats.do: click Approve, wait for the confirmation, highlight it

beats.say: It does the work, but every refund waits for a human.
beats.do: highlight the whole chat

beats.say: In week two, my assistant answered questions from the help center. This week, the agent takes actions on real bookings.
beats.do: open How this works

beats.say: It verifies identity, looks up bookings, checks policy as code, quotes exact amounts, waits for approval, recovers from failures, and remembers.
beats.do: tour the read tools, write tools, numbers, hand-off and memory rows

beats.say: I built it with LangChain and LangGraph. A LangGraph interrupt pauses every write for approval, and a checkpointer gives each chat its memory.
beats.do: highlight the LangGraph flow, close the modal and reset the chat

beats.say: Next, a change that costs money. Maria wants to move her booking to a different flight on November third.
beats.do: type the CLSCHG change request, send

beats.say: The card breaks it down: a seventy five dollar change fee, and a cheaper new fare whose difference SkyClassic does not refund.
beats.do: wait for the approval card (confirm if the agent asks first), highlight the breakdown

beats.say: This time I reject it. Nothing is rebooked, and the agent tells Maria the truth. It never claims the change went through.
beats.do: click Reject, wait for the reply, highlight it

beats.say: Kenji's flight was moved by ninety five minutes. He asks to switch to another flight at no cost.
beats.do: reset the chat, click the Change flight tile, send

beats.say: Over ninety minutes, the schedule change rule makes rebooking free. The card shows no charge. I will leave it waiting for the supervisor.
beats.do: wait for the card, highlight the headline, the waived line and the Waiting state

beats.say: Now, failures. In the demo controls, I take the quote service down. Then Linh asks what she would get back if she cancelled.
beats.do: new chat, open demo controls, select Quote service down, close the drawer, type the LTEXPD question, send

beats.say: The agent retries the quote, it still fails, so it gives no price at all. It hands Linh to a person instead of guessing.
beats.do: wait for the reply, highlight the failed quote step, then the hand-off card

beats.say: This was my instructor's feedback on week two: never keep a price you cannot verify.
beats.do: highlight the hand-off reason

beats.say: Next, a timeout that a retry can fix. The booking lookup will time out once, and Maria asks about a late flight.
beats.do: reset the chat, select Booking lookup times out once, type the DLY3H2 question, send

beats.say: The lookup timed out, the agent retried, and this badge shows it recovered. The conversation just carries on.
beats.do: wait for the reply, highlight the retry badge

beats.say: Over three hours late, for a cause the airline controls: the policy tier is a one hundred dollar travel credit, checked against our systems.
beats.do: highlight the reply, then the figures-checked pill

beats.say: Some requests should never be automated. Emre's father has died, and he needs to cancel.
beats.do: reset the chat, type the BRVMNT message, send

beats.say: A guard catches it before any model call. There is no automated decision. It goes straight to the Care Team, at high priority.
beats.do: wait for the reply, highlight the hand-off card

beats.say: Last, Rana tries to talk her way past the rules. She says she is the supervisor, and the refund is already approved.
beats.do: reset the chat, type the FLXRFD injection, send

beats.say: Her words are only text. The refund still stops at an approval card, and only a real supervisor can decide it.
beats.do: wait for the card, highlight its Waiting state and buttons

beats.say: This is the supervisor page. Pending approvals from every chat wait here: Kenji's free rebooking, and Rana's refund.
beats.do: open /supervisor, tour the two pending items

beats.say: I approve Kenji's rebooking, and the agent replies to him. I reject Rana's refund. Nothing moved without a person.
beats.do: Approve SCH95M, wait for the reply; Reject FLXRFD

beats.say: To grade it, I wrote twenty four multi step scenarios with scripted supervisor decisions and injected faults, each on a fresh database.
beats.do: open the grading card, highlight the suite tile

beats.say: Honestly, the first live run with G P T four point one mini scored sixteen of twenty four.
beats.do: highlight the first-run tile

beats.say: General fixes, none keyed to a single scenario, brought it to twenty three and twenty four of twenty four over two passes.
beats.do: highlight the final tile

beats.say: Zero writes without approval. Policy correctness one hundred percent. Recovery under faults three of three. And two hundred thirty five policy tests pass.
beats.do: tour the safety tiles

beats.say: Each task costs about a third of a cent, and a turn takes about three seconds.
beats.do: highlight the cost tile

beats.say: My week one Agent Report Card graded the logs too: zero critical findings under the project policy.
